reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that thermal aging at 700°C causes trace interstitial-driven phase segregation and softening in a TiVNbTa RHEA, but it does not involve mechanical loading, does not demonstrate brittle precipitates (α-Ti is not shown to be brittle), and reports softening rather than embrittlement or toughness loss. Thus, the key premises linking stress-enhanced diffusion to brittle phase formation and toughness reduction are unsupported by the cited studies.
premises: Stress-enhanced atomic mobility drives localized segregation at elevated temperatures
Trace impurities or elemental segregation lead to formation of brittle precipitates
Brittle precipitates reduce plastic deformation ability and toughness
The initial single-phase HEA has high ductility/toughness
The mechanism operates under demanding mechanical loading at 600–800°C
